subject: MSA + Order Form: carve-out language for consequential / special damages
messages:

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines

Soojin — attaching our consolidated redline (pdf). Two quick asks from procurement/legal: 1) We need the MSA to keep a one-way exclusion for consequential/special/incidental damages in our favor (to avoid uncapped downstream exposure). 2) We accept the proposed mutual cap at $5M in the Order Form but want an exception for data breach and willful misconduct.

Attached: ACME_MSA_v3_redline.pdf

Can your team confirm whether Redwood will accept one-way exclusion limited to downstream customers only (i.e., Acme cannot claim special/consequential from its customers) and whether you can preserve the carve-out to the cap for security incidents?

Jordan — thanks for the redline. Laura and Marcus are looped for legal/ops input; copying our GC Rishi for guidance on exposure. Quick read: 1) One-way exclusions are a common Acme ask but create downstream risk asymmetry for us (customers could pursue consequential damages indirectly tied to our service). 2) We typically accept mutual exclusions with specific carve-outs (IP infringement, gross negligence/willful misconduct, data breach). 3) For security carve-outs we want clear definitions and triggers so the exception to the cap is narrow and measurable.

Action items: Laura — can you propose a bridge clause that preserves Acme's commercial request while limiting Redwood's open exposure? Marcus — ops/eng to confirm detection/notification SLAs that would trigger the security carve-out. Rishi — please weigh in on whether we can accept a one-way exclusion in limited circumstances.

— Soojin
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Teresa Park <legal@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form redlines — proposed compromise language

Team / Jordan — draft compromise below (in plain text so you can paste into your redline):

"Limitation/Exclusion Bridge Proposal"
1) Mutual exclusion: Except for the express exceptions below, neither party shall be liable to the other for special, incidental, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages (including lost profits, loss of business, loss of data or loss of use).
2) Carve-outs (exceptions to limitations and caps): Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party shall remain liable for: (a) damages arising from a grossly negligent act or willful misconduct; (b) claims of intellectual property infringement; (c) direct damages resulting from an unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data, provided that Customer has complied with its obligations under Section X (Incident Response & Notification); and (d) amounts payable under indemnities.
3) Cap interaction: For the avoidance of doubt, damages for items in (2) shall not be subject to the monetary cap in the Order Form.

Rationale: This keeps the exclusion mutual (which Redwood prefers operationally), preserves Acme's desire for protection against third-party downstream damages by limiting the carve-outs to narrow, high-severity exceptions, and links the security carve-out to objective incident-response behavior.

Jordan/Teresa — if Acme needs a one-way exclusion for sales/pipeline reasons, consider a commercial concession (higher cap or warranty credits) in exchange.

—Laura
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Teresa Park <legal@acme.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines — proposed compromise language

Laura — appreciate the quick draft. A few replies from Acme Legal: 1) Mutual exclusion as drafted is workable but Acme requires the ability to recover consequential damages that Acme itself incurs from its downstream customers where such damages are directly attributable to Redwood’s failure to meet material obligations (e.g., prolonged outage causing widespread SLA misses). 2) We don't insist on uncapped exposure for security incidents; we want the security carve-out to be tied to documented regulatory fines and direct remediation costs, not speculative lost profits. 3) Regarding the door you left open for commercial consideration, Jordan and I will evaluate potential concessions (term/cap adjustments) if Redwood insists on mutuality.

Can Redwood suggest specific language that defines "directly attributable" and ties the security carve-out to objective metrics (SLA breach duration, regulator notice).

—Teresa
Senior Counsel, Acme Corp

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Teresa Park <legal@acme.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Final proposal and next steps on damages exclusion

Teresa / Jordan — thanks for the clarity. After internal review, Redwood's position: we prefer the mutual-exclusion route but can accept limited one-way relief in a narrowly scoped scenario where Acme can demonstrate (i) a documented downstream contract obligation to a third party that specifically allocates consequential exposure to Acme, and (ii) that Redwood's breach was the proximate cause of that downstream liability (e.g., continuous downtime > 72 hours resulting in termination of a named downstream contract).

Proposed specific mechanics:
- If Acme invokes the one-way carve-out, Acme must provide the downstream contract and a written incident timeline showing causation within 30 days of notice.
- Security carve-out: liability for documented regulatory fines and direct remediation costs (reasonable third-party forensics, customer notifications, mandatory credit monitoring) arising from an unauthorized access event, subject to cap of $10M for such security remediation per incident, and not exceeding the overall Order Form cap for aggregate events unless willful misconduct is established.

If that structure is acceptable, we'll produce redline language and propose a small commercial concession (10% service credit for SLA failures beyond 24 hours) to offset residual risk. Will prepare redline and a summary memo for your procurement.

Next steps: Teresa/Jordan — let us know acceptance of the mechanics by EOD Mon 4/26. If accepted, Laura will circulate the redline and Marcus will confirm SLA measurement tooling for the timeline proof.

—Rishi
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
